extracted.intended_audience: Habitat for Humanity affiliates, marketing/branding staff, designers, and partners responsible for producing communications and ReStore materials
extracted.subtask_description: Brand user guide rules for correct/incorrect use, color, clear space, sizing, translations, co-branding, and ReStore identifier usage for Habitat for Humanity-affiliated entities. Focused on producing print, digital, event, and co-branded materials that respect the global brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited logo manipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: List of specific prohibited alterations to the Habitat logo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the logo as a watermark or background image; do not place the logo on top of a pattern or other busy background; do not add a drop shadow or other effect; do not change the proportions of the logo; do not use non-master colors or change the color pattern of the logo; do not use the logo in grayscale; do not add a tagline to the logo; do not use any previous versions of a Habitat for Humanity logo; do not use any logo or graphic identifier other than the current logo or extensions thereof. Examples of incorrect usage shown: distorted/resized improperly (hold Shift to constrain), drop shadows, outlines, tinting, strokes, reconfiguring elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended logo signature-line formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for the upper and lower signature lines in extended logos and which words may be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature lines must follow the Habitat entity’s legally registered name. The following words may be omitted from signature lines even if present in the legal name: Inc., of, the, in, for. Depending on the entity name format, both upper and lower signature lines may not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized translations and regional variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on translations of the Habitat logo for non-English contexts (Canada, Spanish-, Portuguese-speaking countries, other regions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Globally the primary version of the Habitat logo is English. In Canada an authorized translation may be used; Quebec affiliates should use French or French-dominant logos where appropriate. In Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking countries, authorized translations may be used. All requests for translated logos must be approved by Habitat for Humanity International’s Marketing, Branding and Publications department (email marketing@habitat.org).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global logo use restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction on use of the global Habitat for Humanity logo by local affiliates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The global Habitat logo (the logo that does not specify an entity’s name) is reserved for Habitat for Humanity International and MUST NOT be used by Habitat-branded entities without express permission from Habitat for Humanity International.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary logo color guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Which colors to use for the Habitat logo and which colors to avoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Habitat logo should be primarily expressed in one color, using master colors black and white for compatibility with the brand palette. The bright blue and bright green in the creative color palette (PANTONE® 638 and 382) should NOT be applied to the Habitat logo. Black logo is preferred on white or light backgrounds; white (reversed) logo may be used on sufficiently dark photographic images or brand-colored backgrounds that are not too busy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-color and traditional blue treatment applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use the two-color Habitat logo or the traditional blue treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the two-color logo for exterior signage, truck wraps, and other physical large-format applications (financial investments). For any printed/produced piece use CMYK or Pantone; for web/digital use RGB values or hex codes. For smaller interior items (business cards, letterhead) you may use either the traditional two-color logo or an all-black version — choose one and be consistent. Traditional blue may be used where a one-color logo is desirable. Using two-color or blue with the new creative color palette is not recommended in general; defined applications exist in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum clear space (print)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required clear space around the Habitat logo to maintain visual integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideal clear space is equal to 2H (twice the height of the “H” in “Habitat”); minimum required clear space is equal to 1H (the height of the “H”). When using the logo at minimum size, allow a minimum of 2H clear space around the logo. Clear space must be free of other graphic elements (typography, icons, other devices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum print sizes for Habitat logo
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum reproduction sizes for primary and alternate logo formats in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary horizontal logo minimum width: 1.125 inches (1 1/8" / 2.86 cm). Vertical logo minimum width: 0.625 inches (5/8" / 1.59 cm). Single-line logo minimum width: 1.8125 inches (1 13/16" / 4.6 cm). When using logo at minimum size, maintain required clear space (2H preferred). Refer to 'Our ReStores' section for specific ReStore identifier minimum sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital/electronic minimum size
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum size requirement for digital/electronic use of the Habitat logo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the Habitat logo online, in social media or other electronic formats, the minimum height of the “H” in “Habitat” should be no less than 10 pixels. All other logo guidelines (clear space, color, integrity) apply online as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program, event and initiative logo usage
rubrics_metrics.description: How to present the Habitat logo in materials for programs, events and initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Habitat logo must stand alone — graphic identifiers, type lockups, or program-specific logo lockups are prohibited (except the Habitat ReStore identifier). Place the Habitat logo prominently above the program, event or initiative name (the name is never placed adjacent to the logo; always beneath). Use a simple and consistent headline treatment (lead with logo, then headline). Headline type: Neue Haas Grotesk Display Medium (approved colors). Supporting text: Neue Haas Grotesk Text Regular (approved colors). In body copy, precede program/event/initiative names on first reference with 'Habitat for Humanity’s' or 'Habitat’s' to reinforce brand ownership. Example sentences provided in guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting graphics limits for programs/events
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on supporting/secondary graphics for program and event materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited supporting/secondary graphics may be created for program/event T-shirts, but should never be applied across the full spectrum of print and online communications. All program/event materials should be created using the creative platform in this guide. Do not use program-specific graphic identifiers as general brand elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-branding: color and general approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred color approach and general guidance for co-branded materials with partners/sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A common, one-color expression is preferred for both logos to reduce complexity and provide equal visual weight. If a partner logo must be in color, use a one-color expression of the Habitat logo in all Habitat-produced materials and publications. Partner use of the traditional two-color Habitat logo on their own materials can be considered case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-sponsor lockup and acknowledgment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: How to recognize a single sponsor and when lockups are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a single sponsor must be recognized but does not qualify for lockup status, lead with the Habitat logo and place sponsor acknowledgment at the bottom of the layout. Single-sponsor lockups (partner logo adjacent to Habitat logo) are reserved for significant contributors. No more than one partner may exist in a co-branded lockup. Lockups should be horizontal with a separating rule; vertical format acceptable only when horizontal format will not work (limited space). When a partner lockup is used, do not also lead with the Habitat logo elsewhere on the same page/layout; instead place the lockup at the bottom and use the 'Habitat for Humanity’s' prefix in headlines. Special exceptions can be discussed by emailing marketing@habitat.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tagline usage in partner lockups
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions and one permitted exception for taglines/slogans in partnership lockups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from using taglines or slogans to supplement the visual identity of partnerships. The single exception: a statement celebrating length of partnership may be presented in the partner logo lockup using only the approved language (e.g., 'Partners in building since 19XX'). When used, this statement is placed one x measurement below the logo separator line, sized to 1/2 x, set in Neue Haas Grotesk Text Bold and centered on the separator line; reserve for significant long-term partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple sponsors guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: How to present multiple sponsor logos and sponsor lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer recognizing multiple corporate sponsors by including their logos together in a linear manner, spaced equally apart without separating rules. Habitat logo should be emphasized and should not be locked up with the grouping of corporate sponsors. Sponsors' logos should be visually equal in size; for tiered sponsorships identify levels and give prominence accordingly. When listing sponsors in type (no logos), set each sponsor name in Neue Haas Grotesk Text Regular (same point size) separated by commas. The words 'Sponsored by:' or 'Sponsors:' can precede the list and should be set in Neue Haas Grotesk Text Bold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use ReStore identifier elements separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on separating elements of the Habitat ReStore identifier or using them as independent graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Habitat ReStore identifier includes the Habitat logo and the ReStore type treatment (including the recycle-house “O” graphic and registered marks). The ReStore identifier and its elements (including the recycle house “O”) MUST NOT be used separately. Do not repeat the identifier in a pattern, use it as a background/watermark, add texture or tinting, remove the ®, use previous nontrademarked versions, or reconfigure elements of the identifier. Additional incorrect usage examples are provided in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitat ReStore extended identifier rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When affiliates may use an extended Habitat ReStore identifier and required exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All affiliates may optionally use an extended Habitat ReStore identifier, but two exceptions require its use: (1) when recognizing a local donor or local corporate partner in any way an extended identifier must be used, and (2) when an affiliate’s advertising efforts extend beyond the local geographic service area (print, TV, online/digital), an extended identifier must be used. Extended identifiers can be used on interior/exterior signage, truck wraps, business cards, letterhead, brochures, ads, etc. When multiple affiliates combine efforts regionally, the global ReStore identifier may be used with permission from Habitat for Humanity International; participating affiliates must identify themselves in materials and request permission at restore@habitat.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReStore identifier formats and color guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted formats (stacked/horizontal) and color rules for the Habitat ReStore identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ReStore identifier is available in two formats: stacked (preferred) and horizontal (only when space limits the stacked format, e.g., digital/social uses or small promotional signage). The identifier follows the same color guidelines as the Habitat logo: do not apply bright PANTONE® 638 or 382 to the identifier. Two-color and traditional blue treatments remain defined for certain uses (e.g., exterior signage). Files for both formats and all file types are available in the Resource Warehouse.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReStore identifier clear space and minimum sizes (print)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear space and print minimum widths for the Habitat ReStore identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum clear space for all ReStore identifier versions in print is equal to 2H (twice the height of the 'H'). Minimum width (print): preferred stacked ReStore identifier and extended version = 1.75 inches (4.375 cm); alternative horizontal format minimum width = 2.5 inches (6.35 cm). Refer to the 'Our Logo' section for related logo minimum sizes and clear space when the Habitat logo is used by itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReStore identifier clear space and minimum sizes (digital)
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital/electronic clear space guidance for ReStore identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the Habitat ReStore identifier online, in social media or other electronic formats, all logo guidelines apply. For primary and horizontal ReStore identifiers the minimum required clear space online is equal to the height of the 'H' in the Habitat logotype. (The guide continues with extended-identifier digital clear-space guidance in the following pages.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo symbol-only usage restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which the house graphic (symbol) may be used without the full wordmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the first time the house graphic element (with the human forms inside) may be used alone in limited applications only. Requirements: the house graphic must remain intact with no alterations or additions; the registered trademark symbol (®) must always appear (preferred lower-right corner of the symbol; can be resized/repositioned as necessary); the house graphic should be used as a large, page-dominant element (not as a small decorative icon) and ideally anchored/bleeding off the page; whenever the house graphic is used separately, the complete/intact full logo must also appear as part of the same design. All rules on color, clear space, and logo integrity apply to the house graphic as well. Use this opportunity judiciously and in keeping with the creative platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Files and resources access
rubrics_metrics.description: Where affiliates can obtain logo and ReStore identifier files and further ReStore guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logo and ReStore identifier files (all formats) and additional ReStore resources are available via the Resource Warehouse at my.habitat.org/resourcewarehouse (ReStore category) or by using the 'marketing & branding' icon on My.Habitat. For permissions, translations, or special exceptions, contact marketing@habitat.org or restore@habitat.org as directed in the guide.
